pro_course_detail.title: Learn how to prepare and give presentations, learn how to inspire, motivate and persuade your audience. Learn how to deal with the question and answer sessions afterwards. Plan, react and succeed!
pro_course_detail.description:
This lesson is designed to inspire, encourage and practise oral presentations in English.

Many people experience worry, nerves and fear before giving an oral presentation. This lesson covers a multitude of subjects and gives a taste of just what is possible wih the correct attitude.

We will  start with the preparation which will include:

* Location - size, hotel/conference centre, seating, eating, team building rooms, heating/cooling etc..
* Materials, whiteboard, interactive audience participation
* Resources, finance, support staff, third tier staff, refreshments
* Assistants to collect data
* Advertising
* Costs, sponsors, vip guests 
* Purpose, call to action, monitoring, analysing, reporting. 

The presentation itself will include:

* Dress code, presenter and audience
* Body language, positioning and mimics
* Primary and secondary seating allocation
* Technological aids
* Timing
* Structure
* Intonation, gestures, rule of threes
* Introduction, content, finishing

The question and answer session will include:

* Opening the question and answer session
* Controlling the question and answer session
* Objection handling techniques
* Cherry picking the right individuals for questions
* Introducing and reacting with a ringer
* Offering promotional literature
* Capturing potential client's details afterwards

A good presentation should be structured, informative and have a pre-determined aim. The audience should feel engaged, individually important and leave better informed than when they arrived.

Most importantly, after the presentation the presenter and the supporting team (if applicable) should be able to identify clear successes that were desired beforehand or the failures, if any, that led to a less than perfect performance. Prepare in advance and you will reap myriad rewards.
 
If you need to give or polish up on your oral presentation skills then I can help. I look forward to demonstrating the power of the professional presentation.

pro_course_detail.title: British culture, stereotype, humour, integration, euphemistic language, accents and much more...!
pro_course_detail.description:
An opportunity to discuss the cultural differences between the United Kingdom and the world with a London born native speaker. Whether you are visiting or moving to the UK or just curious, it's always helpful to understand the people behind the language and how we became the way we are.

Learn about the history behind the idioms, set expressions, the social class system that moulds the people, business and successive generations not to mention our rather peculiar sense of humour and etiquette.

The world is a global village nowadays and international business almost demands an appreciation of the culture surrounding any language for seamless and profitable communication. 

Why take this class.....

1.Better Communication: Understanding culture helps you use the language naturally and appropriately.
2.Deeper Connection: It builds stronger relationships by showing respect for traditions and values.
3.Contextual Understanding: Culture shapes idioms, slang, and expressions in the language.
4.Broader Perspective: It opens your mind to different worldviews and ways of thinking.
5.Improved Retention: Cultural knowledge makes language learning more interesting and memorable.

pro_course_detail.description:
In this lesson we will focus on building your vocabulary and confidence to use new words, phrases and idioms naturally and in free flowing conversation. 
Sometimes because we can't prepare before speaking, it means that we only use language we are very comfortable with. Maybe your written English is a much higher level than your spoken English and you want to find a way to connect the two. 
In this lesson I will prepare vocabulary, phrasal verbs and idioms, tailored to your level, around a conversation topic. You will learn the new material and immediately practice using it through guided questions, giving you plenty of opportunity to start to feel natural and comfortable with the new material. This will then flow into more open conversation questions which will allow you to begin to use new material in a more spontaneous manner. 
Optional homework tasks include reading tasks to expand your vocabulary and writing tasks to practice using new material in sentences.
I always provide PDFs for you to have before and after the lesson, and I will always provide plenty of detail and context for new words and phrases and encourage you to use them like a native speaker!

pro_course_detail.title: Proof reading and correction of written work
pro_course_detail.description:
Send me your writing to proof read and correct.     This can be any type of writing - examples include reports, blogs, application forms, letters, presentations, academic or personal written work. I will suggest English language corrections, and/or highlight areas that you need to make clearer.   Note:  I can usually offer session times in addition to those shown on my calendar for OFFLINE proofreading - please just ask me.

Types of sessions (please confirm your preference in a message to me when booking)
1.  One which we both attend at the agreed time, where we can discuss the contents and any corrections during the session, or 
2.  One which you don't attend but instead send your work to me to read alone and return with written suggestions on how to improve issues such as spelling, vocabulary, grammar and structure.   I return the work within 24 hours of the booked session time (unless an earlier time is agreed with you - please just ask if you need this).
